# WildGaussians


## Overview
WildGaussians is a method for "in-the-wild" 3D reconstruction that integrates robust DINO features and a lightweight appearance modeling module within the 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework to handle unconstrained photo collections [S1][S2, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from standard 3DGS by explicitly addressing varying illumination, occlusions, and transient objects found in real-world data, while maintaining real-time rendering speeds [S1][S2, unofficial].

## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:** Inputs are unconstrained photo collections [S1][S2, unofficial]. Outputs are optimized 3D Gaussians representing the scene [S1][S2, unofficial].

**Data Structures:** The method extends the standard 3DGS Gaussian representation [G]. It incorporates robust DINO features and a lightweight appearance modeling module to handle photometric variations and local appearance details [S1][S2, unofficial].

**Steps:** The sources do not provide a step-by-step algorithm [S1][S2, unofficial]. The method operates within the standard 3DGS training loop, incorporating DINO feature extraction and appearance modeling [S1][S2, unofficial].

**Formulas:** Not given in the sources [S1][S2, unofficial].

**Parameters:** Not given in the sources [S1][S2, unofficial].

**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:** The method is designed to handle occlusions, transient objects, and varying illumination [S1][S2, unofficial]. Specific precision trade-offs or failure modes are not detailed in the sources [S1][S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Dynamic Appearance Features Modeling](3776-dynamic-appearance-features-modeling.md)
Addresses the limitation of global feature embeddings in 3DGS by extracting dynamic appearance features from a reference image to capture local details like highlights and shadows. It sets itself apart from NeRF-W and Ha-NeRF (global embeddings) and CR-NeRF (2D-level features). Choose it when local appearance variations require more than global scene embeddings.

## Operating characteristics
*   **Time Complexity:** Matches real-time rendering speeds of standard 3DGS [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not given in the sources [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **Measured Performance:** Outperforms the original NeRF baseline on wild data and has similar speed to 3DGS on wild data [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **Strengths:** Handles unconstrained photo collections, varying illumination, occlusions, and transient objects [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **Limitations:** Not given in the sources [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **When to use:** When reconstructing scenes from unconstrained, real-world photo collections with varying lighting and potential transients [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **When not to use:** Not given in the sources [S1][S2, unofficial].

## Background
WildGaussians was introduced as part of the effort to extend 3D Gaussian Splatting to "in-the-wild" settings [S1][S2, unofficial]. It addresses the limitations of standard 3DGS, which assumes controlled environments, by integrating robust DINO features and a lightweight appearance modeling module [S1][S2, unofficial]. It is compared with other "in-the-wild" methods like Gaussian in the Wild (GS-W) and Wild-GS [S1][S2, unofficial].
